Heard the parties.

2. The present miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant-Insurance Company against the
Award dated 31.01.2018 passed by the learned District Judge-I- cum-M.A.C.T, Godda in Motor
Branch Manager vs Most. Anita Devi on 13 May, 2024

1

Accident Claim Case No.40 of 2012.
3. It appears that the quantum is not in dispute only right to recovery has been claimed on the ground that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger.
4. The issue has been discussed at paragraph No.19 of the impugned Award, reads as under:-

"19. One argument has been raised by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company at the time of argument that policy does not cover to the deceased as he was gratuitous passenger, but I do not find any substance in this argument on two reasons, firstly, there is no plea by the Insurance Company in his written statement that the deceased was gratuitous passenger and his case is not covered under the policy and secondly, the policy is miscellaneous class D vehicle police- zone C.
The policy covers use of agricultural as well commercial.
The seating capacity is shown 5+1 (including driver) and Rs.50/- has been paid for insurance of driver, conductor and cleaner.
The deceased was engaged as a labour/cleaner on the offending tractor and he was carrying repaired head to the factory.
The tractor was hired by the factory.

Therefore, the deceased was engaged as a labour on the offending tractor, and hence,
I find no reason as to why the case of the deceased shall not be covered under the Insurance policy.
Therefore, I find that the vehicle was duly insured and insurance company could not prove breach of policy condition.
Hence, the insurance company cannot disown its liability for the payment of compensation amount.

Accordingly,
these issues are decided affirmatives."
5. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has submitted that the premium amount has been paid only for driver not for any other passengers.
The compensation amount has already been released in favour of the claimants.

The learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has referred policy, which reads as under:-
"Limitations as to use The policy covers use only under a permit within the meaning of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 or such a carriage failing under sub-section 3 of Section 66 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
1. Use only for agricultural and forestry purpose.
The Police does not cover (1) Use for hire or reward or for racing pace making reliability trial or speed testing.
(2) Use for the carriage of passenger for hire or reward.
(3) Use whilst drawing a greater number of trailers in all than is permitted by law.
2. Use in connection with the insured 6 business.
The police does not cover (1) Use for hire or reward or for racing pace making reliability trial or speed testing.
(2) Use for carriage of passenger for hire or reward.
(3) Use whilst drawing a trailer except the towing (other than for reward) of any one disabled mechanically propelled vehicle."

sentences.text: Admittedly, the vehicle, in question, was being used on hire other than the agricultural purpose.
The deceased was a labourer and he was carrying repaired articles for his company.
Thus, he was simpliciter a passenger.

7. In that view of the matter, this Court finds that the vehicle has been used in an unauthorized manner so far as Insurance Policy is concerned and as such, the owner has no right of indemnification.
Accordingly, right to recovery is granted to the appellant-Insurance Company.
8. With the above modification of the award, the present miscellaneous appeal stands disposed of.
9. The statutory amount shall be remitted to the Tribunal for release of the same either in favour of the claimants or the Insurance Company depending upon the factual matrix of the case.
